name: /onboard
description: Read and understand the codebase before starting work. Builds a working mental model of the project structure, entry points, architecture, and current context.

steps.action: Detect project type and read foundational files
steps.context: Read the project root directory tree (2-3 levels, filenames only). Read whichever exist: package.json, requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, Cargo.toml, go.mod, README.md. Identify: language, framework, package manager, approximate size.
Read whichever exist: Dockerfile, docker-compose*.yml, tsconfig.json, next.config.*, .env.example, Makefile, .github/workflows/*.yml. Identify how the project builds, runs, and deploys.

steps.action: Read entry points and core architecture
steps.context: Based on the detected framework, read the main entry point files and up to 10 core source files. Focus on: API routes/endpoints, service modules, data models/schemas, type definitions. Read signatures and structure, not full implementations. Skip node_modules, .git, __pycache__, dist, build, .next.

steps.description: Load project memory and current context

steps.context: Display a structured summary with: Project name, Stack (language/framework/deps), Structure (how source is organized), Entry points, Key modules, Data (database/storage), Deployment (how it runs), Context (from exocortex files: current work, recent lessons, active tasks). End with: 'Ready to work. What do you need?'
